Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-12

Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Daniel Park (Redwood SE), Sofia Alvarez (Redwood CSM); Rajiv Patel, Emily Turner, Hannah Gold, Marcus Li (LynxCare)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be noisy):
- Purpose: renewal handshake and alignment on multi-region provisioning (EU + US-west) and on-prem pilot timeline; confirm security artifacts for procurement; capacity mapping and latency targets; clarify Dedicated vs Hosted route and failover fallback.
- Outcome: verbal agreement to amend SOW; staging run planned; Redwood to share SOC2/ISO and KMS notes; next provisioning dates set.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we can kick off, um this is Maya on the renewals side from Redwood, Daniel and Sofia from my team, and from LynxCare Rajiv, Emily, Hannah, Marcus. quick agenda — handshake on renewal numbers, map capacity to your QPS, timeline for eu onprem pilot and kms/hsm questions.
[00:28] Rajiv: yeah thanks, yeah hi all. main thing for us is we need to make sure the eu private path is firm — data residency and audit logs, we have a procurement gating checklist that requires SOC two plus iso and a KMS integration. also timeline wise we want the pilot in staging before nov so we can test in production window.
[00:45] Maya: yep totally, we can send SOC 2 and ISO artifact pack. on KMS we support customer-managed KMS via our KMS connector and we can also do HSM where required, it's in the private deployment spec, i'll share the integration notes.
[01:05] Hannah: quick question — for KMS, do you have an automated key rotation story and can we keep keys in our HSM? and what about audit logs retention? procurement asked for 13 months.
[01:20] Daniel: short answer: yes, we support customer KMS; we have a KMS/HSM flow for private and dedicated. rotation can be automated but we can also bring keys to HSM and we log key-use events in audit trail. audit retention defaults to 90 days in hosted but for private we can do custom retention, 13 months is doable, i'll put that on the ticket.
[01:42] Emily: thanks. second, we want to understand the failover behavior; we plan to route to EU primary and fallback to US-west, but we'd like predictable latency. what's the SLO for cross-region fallback?
[01:58] Daniel: fallback adds latency, right — if EU is constrained we can route to a smaller model variant in US-west. typical 95th percentile for fallback is 200 to 350 ms extra depending on model and seq length longer sequences add more. we recommend a canary run. also we can do prefix/KV cash — sorry KV cache — to speed things up, that reduces per-token cost too.
[02:25] Rajiv: ok, good. pricing is also a factor — we were looking at a 20% uplift on current committed capacity, but wondered if dedicated reserved capacity or a hybrid host+dedi approach is better for cost and predictability.
[02:40] Maya: yep, two levers — Redwood Dedicated gives predictability and isolation; Hosted is cheaper for burst. For your QPS and predictable throughput, Dedicated with burst overlay is common. Daniel, you had that mapping?
[02:52] Daniel: right, based on the traffic profile you shared earlier — which was helpful — we estimate 8x A100-equivalent GPUs for the committed footprint to hit your 99k tokens/min target with 95th p99 token latency under the SLO. that'll depend also on quantization and batching settings; we can optimize to reduce cost. i'll attach a mapping spreadsheet.
[03:18] Marcus: can you put that in plain english — 8 GPUs means what in monthly commit dollars and what's the expected headroom?
[03:28] Maya: i'll put numbers in the SOW, rough ballpark immediate commit is — um — $85k/month on dedicated list, with burst credits priced separately. we'll send a firm quote.
[03:40] Rajiv: procurement wants the SOW by friday if possible.
[03:44] Sofia: we can try to get an amended SOW over by friday, need internal approvals but we'll push.
[03:50] Hannah: on security — can we get a redlined datapath diagram for the VPC peering and private control plane? procurement wants network flow diagrams and egress details.
[04:02] Daniel: absolutely, we'll share VPC peering diagrams and egress explanations. note, for on-prem we do a private control plane arrangement and all egress goes through your egress points; we'll document.
[04:18] Emily: great; for the onprem pilot, what's the expected lead time to provision staging nodes in eu?
[04:25] Daniel: typically 10 to 14 business days to provision staging for private, sometimes faster if partner infra is ready. for Dedicated in cloud we can carve out nodes in 3-5 days. since you want both eu private pilot and us-west staging, plan for two-week lead time.
[04:44] Rajiv: fair. we'd like a 48-hour stress run with our traffic pattern and a 7-day soak test. can you support those?
[04:52] Daniel: yes we can run the stress test, we will need the sample traffic profile and a small test harness. Rajiv, if you can provide the 72h profile that'd speed things up.
[04:59] Rajiv: yes i'll share that by monday.
[05:03] Maya: good. i want to call out procurement asks: data residency, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, and SLA lines. we have standard enterprise package and we'll include the SLA amendments.
[05:16] Hannah: the SLA needs a p99 latency target for our key endpoints, and an uptime SLA with credits spelled out. is that standard or do we need an amendment?
[05:26] Sofia: SLA for Dedicated is customizable; we can add p99 latency targets as part of the SOW, that'll be a negotiated clause. we'll capture that in the amendment.
[05:36] Marcus: any competitors offering stricter residency or lower price we should be aware? Rajiv mentioned EdgeServe in procurement shortlist.
[05:44] Maya: competitors are in the list, yes — EdgeServe has low price but less observability; ApexInference pitched lower-latency hardware claims, but our differentiator is the combination of routing, KV cache, and tooling to control unit economics.
[05:58] Rajiv: okay, good. one more — can Redwood support encrypted-at-rest for ephemeral tokens and also ensure minimal logs stored in host region?
[06:06] Daniel: yes, we support encrypted at rest, and we can restrict logs by routing level; for private we can limit retention and region. we'll document the retention config options.
[06:18] Emily: timeline recap?
[06:21] Maya: yep — action items recap: we'll send SOW + pricing by 2026-10-15; Daniel will validate the GPU mapping and attach the capacity spreadsheet by 2026-10-14; we'll send SOC2/ISO pack and KMS notes by 2026-10-14; Rajiv to share 72h traffic profile by 2026-10-18; provision staging nodes by 2026-10-20. plan on an on-prem staging run week of 2026-10-25.
[06:46] Rajiv: sounds good. any blockers?
[06:49] Hannah: procurement needs the KMS HSM note and redlined contract, that's a blocker until we have the redlined SOW.
[06:56] Sofia: we'll prioritize redline and routing to legal; i'll log it as high priority.
[07:02] Marcus: okay thanks, that's helpful.
[07:05] Maya: great, we'll follow up in email and i'll book the on-prem staging slot once provisioning is confirmed. thanks all.

End of call.
